# Wulfcare Data scrapers: full reference for AI agents

Every Actor below runs on Apify. Call: POST {runSyncUrl}?token=APIFY_TOKEN with the JSON input as the body; the response is a JSON array of result items (waits up to 300 s). Longer jobs: POST /v2/acts/{actor}/runs, poll the run, then GET /v2/datasets/{defaultDatasetId}/items. Items with an "error" field are failed rows and are not charged.

---

# Google Trends Scraper: Unlimited Keywords + Daily Data

`wulfcare/google-trends-scraper`: Google Trends without its limits: compare up to 100 keywords on one 0-100 scale (Google stops at 5), and daily data for any range, even 5 years or 2004-now (Google gives weekly/monthly). Plus regions, related queries and Trending Now. Paced so runs finish.

**Use it for:**
- Google Trends interest over time, interest by region, related queries for keywords
- compare more than 5 keywords on one 0-100 scale (up to 100)
- daily Google Trends data for long ranges (12 months, 5 years, 2004-now)
- what is trending on Google right now in a country (Trending Now)
- replacement for pytrends when it fails with 429 TooManyRequestsError

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/google-trends-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-trends-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/google-trends-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.003 per trends report (trends-report): One Explore report: interest over time, interest by region and related queries for up to 5 compared terms.
- $0.0005 per trending search (trending-item): One trending search from Trending Now, with volume, growth, related searches and category.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-trends-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"searchTerms": ["coffee, tea"], "geo": "US", "timeRange": "today 12-m"}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/google-trends-scraper").call(run_input={"searchTerms": ["coffee, tea"], "geo": "US", "timeRange": "today 12-m"})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string |  | "explore" | `explore` (Explore: search terms (interest over time, by region, related queries)), `trendingNow` (Trending Now: what's trending in a country right now) | What to scrape: Explore gives interest over time, by region and related queries for your search terms. Trending Now lists every search trending in the countries you pick. |
| `searchTerms` | array |  |  |  | Search terms: One report per line. Compare terms by separating them with commas, e.g. coffee, tea. No 5-term limit: put up to 100 terms on one line and they all come back on one 0-100 scale (Google itself compares only 5; we chain overlapping groups, charged per Google query used). You can also paste a Google Trends explore URL, and its terms, country, time range and category are used as-is. |
| `geo` | string |  | "" |  | Country or region: ISO country code like US, AU, GB, or a region like US-CA. Leave empty for worldwide. |
| `timeRange` | string |  | "today 12-m" | `now 1-H` (Past hour), `now 4-H` (Past 4 hours), `now 1-d` (Past day), `now 7-d` (Past 7 days), `today 1-m` (Past 30 days), `today 3-m` (Past 90 days), `today 12-m` (Past 12 months), `today 5-y` (Past 5 years), `all` (2004 - present) | Time range: Period to analyse. Google picks the resolution: minutes for the past hour or 4 hours, hours for 7 days, days up to 90 days, weeks up to 5 years, and months since 2004. |
| `customTimeRange` | string |  |  |  | Custom time range (optional): Overrides the time range above. Format YYYY-MM-DD YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. 2024-01-01 2024-06-30. |
| `dailyData` | boolean |  | false |  | Daily data for any time range: Google only gives daily points for ranges under ~9 months, then weekly or monthly. Turn this on to get daily points for the whole range (12 months, 5 years, even 2004 to now): we fetch ~8-month daily windows and scale each one to Google's full-range series. Each window is one more Google query, charged as a report (5 years ≈ 10 reports). Up to 5 terms per line. |
| `category` | integer |  | 0 |  | Category ID: Google Trends category, e.g. 0 = all, 71 = Food & Drink, 7 = Finance. Default 0. |
| `searchProperty` | string |  | "" | `` (Web search), `images` (Image search), `news` (News search), `froogle` (Google Shopping), `youtube` (YouTube search) | Search type: Which Google search to measure: web (default), images, news, Google Shopping or YouTube. |
| `interestOverTime` | boolean |  | true |  | Interest over time: Relative search interest (0-100) over the chosen time range. |
| `interestByRegion` | boolean |  | true |  | Interest by region: Relative search interest (0-100) by country, region, city or US metro area. |
| `relatedQueries` | boolean |  | true |  | Related queries (top + rising): The top and rising searches related to each term, including "Breakout" queries (growth over 5,000%). |
| `regionResolution` | string |  | "" | `` (Google default), `COUNTRY` (Countries), `REGION` (Regions / states), `CITY` (Cities), `DMA` (US metro areas (DMA)) | Region resolution: Level of detail for interest by region. "Google default" uses countries for worldwide and regions within a country. |
| `includeLowVolumeRegions` | boolean |  | false |  | Include low search volume regions: Include regions with too little search volume for Google to rate reliably (they usually show 0). |
| `saveCsv` | boolean |  | true |  | Also save spreadsheet-friendly CSVs: Saves interest_over_time.csv, interest_by_region.csv and related_queries.csv (one row per value) to the run's key-value store for Excel or Google Sheets. Free. |
| `trendingGeos` | array |  |  |  | Countries or regions: ISO codes like US, GB, AU, or regions like US-CA. One set of trends per entry. |
| `trendingHours` | string |  | "24" | `4` (Past 4 hours), `24` (Past 24 hours), `48` (Past 48 hours), `168` (Past 7 days) | Time window: How far back to look for trending searches. |
| `trendingCategories` | array |  |  |  | Only these categories (optional): Leave empty for all categories. |
| `trendingActiveOnly` | boolean |  | false |  | Only trends that are still active: Skip trends that have already ended. |
| `maxTrendsPerGeo` | integer |  | 0 | 0– | Max trends per country (0 = all): Trends are sorted by search volume, highest first. |
| `language` | string |  | "en-US" |  | Interface language: Language of Google's labels and related queries, e.g. en-US, en-GB, de, ja. |
| `timezoneOffsetMinutes` | integer |  | 0 |  | Timezone offset (minutes): Google's tz parameter: minutes WEST of UTC (Sydney = -600, New York = 300). |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 3 | 1–10 | Parallel reports: How many reports run at once, each on its own IP. Only applies when using a proxy. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)

# YouTube Transcript & Subtitle Scraper: Channels & Playlists

`wulfcare/youtube-transcript-scraper`: YouTube transcripts and subtitles as text, timestamped text, segments or SRT for videos, Shorts, channels, playlists and searches. $0.003 each, no-caption videos free. Drop-in for other transcript Actors: same startUrls/timestamps or videoUrl/targetLanguage input and output fields.

**Use it for:**
- transcripts / captions / subtitles of YouTube videos as text, timestamped segments or SRT
- transcripts of every video in a channel, playlist or search
- replacement for youtube-transcript-api when it raises RequestBlocked / IpBlocked
- drop-in replacement for other Apify YouTube transcript/subtitle Actors: accepts startUrls + timestamps and videoUrl + targetLanguage, returns the same fields (videoUrl, videoId, videoTitle, channelName, views, language, text, data) at $0.003 per transcript

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/youtube-transcript-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~youtube-transcript-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/youtube-transcript-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.003 per transcript (transcript): The transcript of one video (text, timestamped segments and optional SRT) with its title, channel, publish date and other details. Videos without captions, unavailable videos, bad inputs and failed requests are never charged.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~youtube-transcript-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"urls": ["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UF8uR6Z6KLc"], "languages": ["en"]}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/youtube-transcript-scraper").call(run_input={"urls": ["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UF8uR6Z6KLc"], "languages": ["en"]})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `urls` | array |  |  |  | Videos, channels or playlists: Any mix of video URLs (watch, youtu.be, Shorts, live, embed), 11-character video ids, channel URLs (@handle, /channel/UC..., /c/..., /user/...) and playlist URLs. Channels and playlists are expanded into their videos, newest first, up to the limit below. |
| `searchQueries` | array |  |  |  | YouTube searches: Optional. Transcripts of the videos YouTube lists for each search term (videos only, YouTube's relevance order). |
| `maxVideosPerSource` | integer |  | 20 | 0– | Max videos per channel, playlist or search: 0 = all of them. Single video URLs are always fetched. |
| `channelTabs` | array |  | ["videos"] |  | Channel tabs: Which of a channel's tabs to take videos from. Each tab counts as its own source for the limit above. |
| `languages` | array |  | ["en"] |  | Transcript language: Language codes in order of preference (en, es, pt-BR, ja...). "en" also matches en-US and en-GB. Captions uploaded by the creator are used before auto-generated ones in the same language. Leave empty to always get the video's original (spoken) language. |
| `ifLanguageMissing` | string |  | "original" | `original` (Use the video's original language), `skip` (Skip the video (free error row)) | If a video has none of these languages: Every row says which language it's in (language, isAutoGenerated) and lists all the video's caption languages (availableLanguages). |
| `includeAutoGenerated` | boolean |  | true |  | Use auto-generated captions: Most videos only have YouTube's automatic (speech recognition) captions. Turn off to accept only captions made by a person. |
| `includeSegments` | boolean |  | true |  | Timestamped segments: segments: [{start, duration, text}] in seconds, as shown on screen. The full transcript is always in text. |
| `includeSrt` | boolean |  | false |  | SRT subtitles: Adds the transcript as an .srt subtitle file (srt field), ready for video editors and players. |
| `timestamps` | boolean |  | false |  | Timestamps in the text: Puts [HH:MM:SS.mmm] at the start of each caption line in text, one line each (handy for LLM prompts and quoting). Off: text is one plain paragraph. |
| `includePublishDate` | boolean |  | true |  | Publish date and category: publishedAt and category, from one extra request per video. Off makes big runs about twice as fast: YouTube limits how many videos one IP address may ask for per minute. |
| `includeDescription` | boolean |  | true |  | Video description: The full description text. Title, channel, duration, views, keywords and thumbnail are always included. |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 5 | 1–20 | Videos at a time: Videos processed at once. YouTube lets each IP address fetch roughly 40-75 videos a minute, so a bigger proxy pool speeds up big runs more than this does. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)

```json
{
  "input": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UF8uR6Z6KLc",
  "videoId": "UF8uR6Z6KLc",
```

# YouTube Scraper: Videos, Shorts, Channels & Search

`wulfcare/youtube-scraper`: YouTube scraper: videos, Shorts and streams from searches, channels, playlists and hashtags. Views, likes, comments count, publish time, duration, tags, plus channel subscribers, total views and country. Same input and output as the popular YouTube Scraper. Free until Nov 18, then $0.90 per 1,000.

**Use it for:**
- YouTube video metadata (views, likes, comment count, publish date, duration, tags) from searches, channels, playlists, hashtags
- YouTube channel stats (subscribers, total views, country)
- YouTube search without YouTube Data API quota

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/youtube-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~youtube-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/youtube-scraper`

**Price:**
- Free (only Apify platform usage, usually fractions of a cent)
- From 2026-11-18: $0.0009 per video (video): One YouTube video, Short or stream row with all its details. Errors and not-found inputs are never charged. No start fee.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~youtube-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"searchQueries": ["python tutorial"], "maxResults": 20}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/youtube-scraper").call(run_input={"searchQueries": ["python tutorial"], "maxResults": 20})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `searchQueries` | array |  |  |  | Search terms: What you would type in YouTube's search box. Each term is searched separately and gets up to "Maximum videos" results (and Shorts / live streams if you ask for them below). |
| `maxResults` | integer |  | 10 | 0–999999 | Maximum videos per search term, channel, playlist or hashtag: Regular videos to get from each search term, channel (its Videos tab), playlist and hashtag. 0 = none. Video URLs in Direct URLs are always scraped. |
| `maxResultsShorts` | integer |  | 0 | 0–999999 | Maximum Shorts per search term or channel: Shorts to get from each search term (YouTube's "Shorts" search filter) and each channel (its Shorts tab). 0 = none. |
| `maxResultStreams` | integer |  | 0 | 0–999999 | Maximum live streams per search term or channel: Live streams to get from each channel (its Live tab: past, current and upcoming streams) and each search term (YouTube's "Live" filter: streams live right now). 0 = none. |
| `startUrls` | array |  | [] |  | Direct URLs: YouTube URLs: videos, Shorts, channels (@handle, /channel/UC..., /c/..., /user/...; a channel tab URL like /@name/shorts gets only that tab), playlists, search result pages (with their filters) and hashtag pages. Bare video ids, @handles and channel ids work too. |
| `sortingOrder` | string |  |  | `relevance` (Relevance), `rating` (Rating), `date` (Upload date), `views` (View count) | Sorting order: How YouTube orders the search results. YouTube doesn't follow "Upload date" strictly. |
| `dateFilter` | string |  |  | `hour` (Last hour), `today` (Today), `week` (This week), `month` (This month), `year` (This year) | Upload date: Only videos uploaded within this time. |
| `videoType` | string |  |  | `video` (Video), `movie` (Movie) | Type: Videos (default) or movies. |
| `lengthFilter` | string |  |  | `under4` (Under 4 minutes), `between420` (4-20 minutes), `plus20` (Over 20 minutes) | Duration: Only videos of this length. |
| `isHD` | boolean |  |  |  | HD: Only videos with the "HD" feature. |
| `hasSubtitles` | boolean |  |  |  | Subtitles/CC: Only videos with the "Subtitles/CC" feature. |
| `hasCC` | boolean |  |  |  | Creative Commons: Only videos with the "Creative Commons" feature. |
| `is3D` | boolean |  |  |  | 3D: Only videos with the "3D" feature. |
| `isLive` | boolean |  |  |  | Live: Only streams that are live now. |
| `isBought` | boolean |  |  |  | Purchased: Only videos with the "Purchased" feature. |
| `is4K` | boolean |  |  |  | 4K: Only videos with the "4K" feature. |
| `is360` | boolean |  |  |  | 360°: Only videos with the "360°" feature. |
| `hasLocation` | boolean |  |  |  | Location: Only videos with the "Location" feature. |
| `isHDR` | boolean |  |  |  | HDR: Only videos with the "HDR" feature. |
| `isVR180` | boolean |  |  |  | VR180: Only videos with the "VR180" feature. |
| `oldestPostDate` | string |  |  |  | Only videos published on or after: A date (2026-01-31) or an age ("7 days", "2 weeks", "3 months", "1 year"). Works for every source. On a channel listed newest first the run stops at the first older video; elsewhere older videos are skipped. |
| `sortVideosBy` | string |  | "NEWEST" | `NEWEST` (Newest), `POPULAR` (Popular), `OLDEST` (Oldest) | Channel order: The order of a channel's videos, Shorts and streams (the channel page's Latest / Popular / Oldest buttons). |
| `includeVideoDetails` | boolean |  | true |  | Open every video (likes, comments, exact date, description, tags...): On: each video's likes, comment count, exact publish time, full description with its links, hashtags, category, tags and more. Off: only what the list shows (title, views, duration, "3 days ago"), several times faster. Video URLs are always opened. |
| `includeChannelInfo` | boolean |  | true |  | Add channel info to each video: The channel's subscribers, total views, video count, country, joined date, description, links, avatar and banner, on every row (one small request per channel). |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 10 | 1–30 | Videos at a time: How many videos are fetched in parallel. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)

# YouTube Comments Scraper: Replies, Likes & Hearts

`wulfcare/youtube-comments-scraper`: Scrape YouTube comments and replies from any video or Short, or from a channel, playlist or search. Text, author, likes, reply count, creator heart, pinned, date and exact comment total. No API key or quota. Same input and output as the popular YouTube Comments Scraper. $0.25 per 1,000 comments.

**Use it for:**
- comments and replies of YouTube videos and Shorts with likes, reply counts, creator hearts, pinned flags and dates
- comments across a channel, playlist or search, optionally only since a date
- YouTube comments for sentiment analysis, brand monitoring or AI datasets, without a YouTube API key or quota
- drop-in replacement for other Apify YouTube comments Actors: accepts startUrls + maxComments + sortCommentsBy and startUrls + sort + maxItems, same output field names as the most used one

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/youtube-comments-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~youtube-comments-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/youtube-comments-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.00025 per comment (comment): One YouTube comment or reply row. Errors, unavailable videos and turned-off comments are never charged. No start fee.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~youtube-comments-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"startUrls": ["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"], "maxComments": 100, "sortCommentsBy": "TOP_COMMENTS"}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/youtube-comments-scraper").call(run_input={"startUrls": ["https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ"], "maxComments": 100, "sortCommentsBy": "TOP_COMMENTS"})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `startUrls` | array |  |  |  | YouTube URLs: Videos or Shorts (one per line; {"url": ...} objects work too) to get comments from (watch, youtu.be, /shorts/ URLs or 11-character video IDs). Channel URLs (@handle, /channel/UC...; add /shorts for Shorts), playlist URLs and search result URLs also work: their newest/first "Maximum videos" videos are used. |
| `maxComments` | integer |  | 100 | 0–1000000 | Maximum comments per video: Comments (and replies, when on) to get from each video. 0 = all of them. ~1,000 comments take about 20 seconds. |
| `sortCommentsBy` | string |  | "NEWEST_FIRST" | `TOP_COMMENTS` (Top comments), `NEWEST_FIRST` (Newest first) | Sort comments by: YouTube's own Top / Newest order. |
| `includeReplies` | boolean |  | false |  | Include replies: Also get the replies to each comment, right after it (type "reply", replyToCid = the comment). Replies count toward "Maximum comments". |
| `maxRepliesPerComment` | integer |  | 0 | 0–100000 | Maximum replies per comment: 0 = all replies of each comment. |
| `oldestCommentDate` | string |  |  |  | Only comments posted on or after: A date (2026-01-31) or an age ("7 days", "3 months"). With "Newest first" the run stops reading a video once comments get older. YouTube only says "x days ago", so the cut is approximate. |
| `searchQueries` | array |  |  |  | Search terms: Get comments from the top "Maximum videos" YouTube search results of each term (e.g. a product or brand name). |
| `maxVideos` | integer |  | 10 | 1–10000 | Maximum videos per channel, playlist or search: How many videos each channel (newest first), playlist or search term contributes. |
| `maxItems` | integer |  |  | 1–10000000 | Maximum comments in total: Optional cap for the whole run (all videos together). Empty = no cap. |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 5 | 1–20 | Videos at a time: How many videos are read in parallel. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)

```json
{
  "comment": "(comment text removed)",
  "cid": "Ugxzbv_ZeZXNRcfwsSF4AaABAg",
  "author": "(name removed)",
  "videoId": "dQw4w9WgXcQ",
  "pageUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ",
  "commentsCount": 2461305,
  "replyCount": 726,
  "voteCount": 293000,
  "authorIsChannelOwner": false,
  "hasCreatorHeart": false,
  "type": "comment",
  "replyToCid": null,
  "title": "Rick Astley - Never Gonna Give You Up (Official Video) (4K Remaster)",

  "isEdited": false,
  "isPinned": false,
  "replyLevel": 0,
```

# Google Jobs Scraper: Salaries, Descriptions & Apply Links

`wulfcare/google-jobs-scraper`: Scrape Google Jobs: title, company, location, salary, job type, posted date, full description, highlights and every real apply link (LinkedIn, Indeed, company site...). Up to 200 unique jobs per search, 27 countries.

**Use it for:**
- job listings from Google Jobs (Google for Jobs) with salary, description and apply links

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/google-jobs-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-jobs-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/google-jobs-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.004 per job posting (google-job): One unique Google Jobs posting with title, company, location, salary, type, description, highlights and apply links. Duplicates are never charged.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-jobs-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"queries": ["data analyst jobs london"], "country": "GB", "maxJobsPerQuery": 30}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/google-jobs-scraper").call(run_input={"queries": ["data analyst jobs london"], "country": "GB", "maxJobsPerQuery": 30})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `queries` | array | yes |  |  | Searches: What you'd type into Google, one per line, e.g. data analyst jobs london or remote python developer. Include the place in the search. |
| `country` | string |  | "US" | `US` (United States), `GB` (United Kingdom), `IE` (Ireland), `CA` (Canada), `DE` (Germany), `AT` (Austria), `CH` (Switzerland), `FR` (France), `BE` (Belgium), `NL` (Netherlands), `ES` (Spain), `PT` (Portugal), `IT` (Italy), `PL` (Poland), `SE` (Sweden), `NO` (Norway), `DK` (Denmark), `FI` (Finland), `IN` (India), `SG` (Singapore), `AE` (United Arab Emirates), `ZA` (South Africa), `BR` (Brazil), `MX` (Mexico), `JP` (Japan), `AU` (Australia (limited)), `NZ` (New Zealand (limited)) | Country: Which country's Google to search. Google Jobs isn't offered for every country; Australia and New Zealand usually return no jobs view. |
| `maxJobsPerQuery` | integer |  | 30 | 1–200 | Max jobs per search: Unique jobs to return per search. Google shows 10 at a time, so more than 10 needs 'Expand results'. |
| `expandResults` | boolean |  | true |  | Expand results: Google only shows 10 jobs per search. This runs natural variations (full time, senior, posted this week, remote...) and removes duplicates, for typically 40-80 unique jobs per search. You're only charged for unique jobs. |
| `includeDescription` | boolean |  | true |  | Include full job description: The full posting text. Turn off for smaller, faster output. |
| `language` | string |  | "en" |  | Language: Google interface language, e.g. en, de, fr, es. |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 3 | 1–10 | Parallel searches: How many Google searches run at once. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)


# Google Hotels Prices Scraper

`wulfcare/google-hotels-scraper`: Hotel prices from Google Hotels: every booking site's price (Booking.com, Expedia, Agoda, the hotel's own site...) for any hotel and dates, per night and total, with and without taxes, plus hotel searches like "hotels in Paris" with ratings, stars, address and lowest price. $0.80 per 1,000 prices.

**Use it for:**
- hotel prices from every booking site (Booking.com, Expedia, Agoda, official site) for given dates
- hotel price calendar over many check-in dates
- list of hotels in a city with rating, stars and lowest price

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/google-hotels-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-hotels-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/google-hotels-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.0008 per price (price): One booking site's price for one hotel and one check-in date (per night and total, with and without taxes, booking link). Dates without prices and errors are never charged.
- $0.0015 per hotel from a search (hotel): One hotel from a Google Hotels search, with its details (stars, rating, reviews, address, location, photos) and lowest price.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-hotels-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"hotels": ["Hilton London Paddington"], "checkInDate": "+30 days", "nights": 2, "adults": 2, "currency": "USD"}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/google-hotels-scraper").call(run_input={"hotels": ["Hilton London Paddington"], "checkInDate": "+30 days", "nights": 2, "adults": 2, "currency": "USD"})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hotels` | array |  |  |  | Hotels: Hotels to get every booking site's prices for. Each one can be a hotel's name (best with the city: "Hilton London Paddington"), a Google Hotels link (https://www.google.com/travel/hotels/entity/...) or its entity ID (the "Ch..." code in that link), or the hotel's Google Maps link or CID. |
| `searchQueries` | array |  |  |  | Searches: Google Hotels searches, e.g. "hotels in Paris" or "beach hotels in Bali". Each gives one row per hotel (name, stars, rating, reviews, address, lowest price and more), up to "Maximum hotels per search". |
| `maxHotels` | integer |  | 20 | 1–1000 | Maximum hotels per search: Hotels to get from each search, in Google's order. |
| `includeAllPrices` | boolean |  | false |  | Every booking site's price for searched hotels: Searches give each hotel's lowest price. Turn this on to also get every booking site's price for each hotel found (in its "prices" list, charged per price). |
| `checkInDate` | string |  |  |  | Check-in date: First check-in date (YYYY-MM-DD, or "tomorrow", "+7 days"). Empty = tomorrow. Google has prices for about a year ahead. |
| `days` | integer |  | 1 | 1–365 | Check-in dates: How many check-in dates in a row, from the first: 30 gives a price calendar for the next 30 check-ins. |
| `nights` | integer |  | 1 | 1–30 | Nights: Length of each stay. |
| `adults` | integer |  | 2 | 1–10 | Adults: Guests. Prices and the booking sites offering them change with the number of guests. |
| `currency` | string |  | "USD" |  | Currency: Three-letter code (USD, EUR, GBP, AUD...). Google prices in the currency of the country the request comes from (USD with the default US proxy); other currencies are converted at the day's ECB reference rate. For prices exactly as shown in a country (local currency and taxes), use a residential proxy from that country. |
| `outputFormat` | string |  | "providers" | `providers` (One row per booking site and date), `hotels` (One row per hotel and date (prices in a list)) | Output: How rows for the hotels above come out. Searches always give one row per hotel. |
| `device` | string |  | "desktop" | `desktop` (Desktop), `mobile` (Mobile) | Device: Get the prices Google shows on desktop or on mobile (some sites have mobile-only rates). |
| `language` | string |  | "en" |  | Language: Language of hotel descriptions and texts (en, fr, de, es...). |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 6 | 1–20 | Parallel requests: Requests to Google at once. |
| `entity` | string |  |  |  | Entity (compatibility): A single hotel (entity ID, link or name): same as one line in Hotels. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)


# Google Flights Scraper & Price Tracker

`wulfcare/google-flights-scraper`: Google Flights prices for any route and date, with price tracking built in: each run says which prices dropped or rose, which flights are new or gone, and the all-time low. Plus total trip cost with a hotel, cheapest dates, layovers, CO2 and Google's low/typical/high verdict. Built for AI agents.

**Use it for:**
- Google Flights prices for any route and date with airlines, times, layovers and CO2
- whether a fare is good: Google's low / typical / high verdict, typical price range and price history
- flight price tracking between runs: drops, rises, new and gone flights, all-time low
- total trip cost: flight plus the cheapest well-rated hotel
- cheapest price for every departure date in a range

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/google-flights-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-flights-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/google-flights-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.0005 per result (result): One row: a summary of a route and date (lowest price, Google's low/typical/high verdict, price changes since the last run, trip cost with hotel), one flight, or one date's cheapest price. Errors and 'gone' rows are free; hotel lookups are included.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-flights-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"origin": "JFK", "destination": "LAX", "departureDate": "+30 days", "maxFlights": 5}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/google-flights-scraper").call(run_input={"origin": "JFK", "destination": "LAX", "departureDate": "+30 days", "maxFlights": 5})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `origin` | string |  |  |  | From (airport code): IATA code of the departure airport, e.g. JFK. Several, comma-separated, to search them together: JFK,LGA,EWR. |
| `destination` | string |  |  |  | To (airport code): IATA code of the arrival airport, e.g. LAX (or several: LAX,BUR,LGB). |
| `departureDate` | string |  |  |  | Departure date: YYYY-MM-DD, or relative: "+30 days", "in 2 weeks", "tomorrow". Empty = in 30 days. |
| `returnDate` | string |  |  |  | Return date (round trip): Empty = one way. YYYY-MM-DD, or "+7 days" counted from the departure date. Round-trip prices are for the whole trip, as on Google Flights. |
| `tripDays` | integer |  |  | 0–330 | Trip length in days (round trip): Instead of a return date: return this many days after departure. 0 = one way. |
| `routes` | array |  |  |  | More routes: Extra routes, one per line: "SYD-LAX", "JFK,EWR-LHR", "MEL to AKL". Each is searched for the same dates and options. |
| `departureDays` | integer |  | 1 | 1–60 | Departure dates in a row: Search this many consecutive departure dates from the first (full flight lists for each). For just the cheapest price per date over a long range, use "Cheapest dates" instead. |
| `maxFlights` | integer |  | 20 | 0–500 | Flights per search: Flight rows per route and date: Google's "best" flights first, then the rest by price. Google lists 50-300. 0 = just the summary row (lowest price, verdict, trip cost). |
| `cabinClass` | string |  | "economy" | `economy` (Economy), `premium-economy` (Premium economy), `business` (Business), `first` (First) | Cabin: Seat class. |
| `adults` | integer |  | 1 | 1–9 | Adults: Prices are the total for all passengers. |
| `children` | integer |  | 0 | 0–8 | Children (2-11): Children aged 2-11 (count toward the total price). |
| `maxStops` | string |  | "any" | `any` (Any), `nonstop` (Nonstop only), `1` (1 stop or fewer), `2` (2 stops or fewer) | Stops: Most stops a flight may have. |
| `currency` | string |  | "USD" |  | Currency: Three-letter code: USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, INR... Google prices directly in it. |
| `trackPrices` | boolean |  | false |  | Track prices between runs: Remember this run's prices and compare the next run with them: every flight gets priceStatus (new, cheaper, pricier, same), previousPrice, priceChange and its lowest price seen; flights no longer listed come out as "gone" (free); the summary gets the change in the lowest price and the all-time low. Schedule the Actor (e.g. daily) with the same input. Prices are kept in your named key-value store "google-flights-tracker-". |
| `trackerName` | string |  | "default" |  | Tracker name: Keep separate trackers apart (e.g. "client-a", "summer-trip"). Letters, digits, dashes. |
| `onlyChanges` | boolean |  | false |  | Only output changes: With tracking: output only flights that are new or changed price (plus one summary row per search). You pay only for those rows, so daily monitoring costs almost nothing. |
| `targetPrice` | integer |  |  | 0– | Target price: Optional: the summary's belowTargetPrice is true when the lowest price is at or under this (in the chosen currency). Handy for alerts and webhooks. |
| `includeHotels` | boolean |  | false |  | Add hotel and total trip cost: Look up the cheapest well-rated hotel (3+ stars, 4+ rating by default) in the destination city on Google Hotels for the stay (arrival to return date, or "Hotel nights" for one way), and add tripTotalPrice = flight + hotel to the summary and every flight. No extra charge. |
| `hotelNights` | integer |  | 3 | 1–30 | Hotel nights (one way): Stay length for one-way searches. Round trips stay until the return date. |
| `hotelMinRating` | string |  | "4" | `0` (Any), `3.5` (3.5+), `4` (4+), `4.5` (4.5+) | Hotel minimum rating: Google rating (out of 5) a hotel needs to count. |
| `hotelMinStars` | integer |  | 3 | 0–5 | Hotel minimum stars: Hotel class a hotel needs to count (0 = any). Hostels, dorms and apartments never count, so the trip cost is for a real hotel room. |
| `cheapestDates` | boolean |  | false |  | Cheapest dates: Also output the cheapest price for every departure date in a range (Google's date grid), one row per date, the cheapest flagged. Round trips keep the same trip length. |
| `cheapestDatesRange` | integer |  | 60 | 7–330 | Days to scan: Departure dates from the departure date on. |
| `language` | string |  | "en" |  | Language: Language of airport and airline names (hl=). |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 6 | 1–20 | Requests at once: Searches sent to Google at the same time. |
| `residentialFallback` | boolean |  | true |  | Fall back to residential proxy: With the default Apify Proxy: when Google keeps refusing datacenter IPs, finish the run on US residential IPs (no extra charge to you). |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)

```json
{
```

# App Store Scraper: Reviews, App Details, Search & Charts

`wulfcare/app-store-scraper`: Scrape Apple App Store reviews with no 500 cap (any country, newest/helpful/critical sort, star and date filters, developer replies), full app details with rating histogram, version history and App Privacy labels, search results, top charts, developer apps and similar apps.

**Use it for:**
- Apple App Store app details, rating histogram, version history, privacy labels
- App Store search results, top charts, developer apps, similar apps
- App Store reviews together with app data

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/app-store-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~app-store-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/app-store-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.0001 per review (review): One App Store review with stars, title, text, date, the developer reply and (for recent reviews) the app version. Not-found apps and failed requests are never charged.
- $0.0005 per app details (app-details): Full details of one app: rating histogram, price, in-app purchases, version history, age rating, privacy labels, chart position and more.
- $0.0002 per app in a list (app-list-item): One app from a search, top chart, developer page or similar-apps list, with title, rating, price, category and description.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~app-store-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"mode": "apps", "appIds": ["324684580"], "countries": ["us"]}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/app-store-scraper").call(run_input={"mode": "apps", "appIds": ["324684580"], "countries": ["us"]})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | yes | "reviews" | `reviews` (Reviews of apps), `apps` (App details (full)), `search` (Search results), `charts` (Top charts), `developer` (Apps by developer), `similar` (Similar apps (You Might Also Like)) | What to scrape: Each run returns one kind of row, so your dataset always has the same columns. Reviews, App details and Similar apps use the app list below; the other modes use their own section. |
| `appIds` | array |  |  |  | Apps: App Store URLs (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/.../id324684580), numeric app ids (324684580) or bundle ids (com.spotify.client). Used by Reviews, App details and Similar apps. |
| `countries` | array |  | ["us"] |  | Countries: Two-letter App Store country codes (us, gb, de, jp, br, ...). Each country is its own store with its own reviews, prices, charts and search results; add several to cover them all in one run. Every row says which country it came from. |
| `language` | string |  |  |  | Language: Optional, e.g. en-US, de-DE, fr-FR. App names and descriptions come in this language when the developer provides it. Leave empty for each country's default language. Reviews are always the ones written in that country's store, whatever their language. |
| `maxReviewsPerApp` | integer |  | 100 | 0– | Max reviews per app: 0 = every review the App Store has for the app in each country (no 500 cap). With a star filter, this counts only reviews with those stars. |
| `reviewsSort` | string |  | "newest" | `newest` (Newest first), `helpful` (Most helpful (App Store default)), `favorable` (Most favorable (5 stars first)), `critical` (Most critical (1 star first)) | Sort reviews by: Newest first is best for monitoring and date cutoffs. Most critical is the fastest way to get complaints. |
| `reviewStars` | array |  |  |  | Only these star ratings: Leave empty for all ratings. You're only charged for reviews with these stars. Tip: with Most critical (or Most favorable) the run stops as soon as it's past the stars you picked. |
| `reviewsSince` | string |  |  |  | Only reviews since: Skip reviews older than this, e.g. 2026-09-01 or "30 days". With Newest first the run stops as soon as it reaches older reviews. |
| `includeReviewerNames` | boolean |  | false |  | Include reviewer nicknames: Off by default. The App Store shows a nickname for each reviewer; no other reviewer data is collected. |
| `searchQueries` | array |  |  |  | Search terms: One search per line, e.g. "habit tracker". Up to 200 apps per term and country. |
| `chartCollections` | array |  | ["topfree"] |  | Charts: Which top charts to fetch (up to 100 apps each, Apple's limit). |
| `chartDevice` | string |  | "iphone" | `iphone` (iPhone), `ipad` (iPad), `mac` (Mac) | Chart device: iPhone, iPad or Mac App Store charts. |
| `chartGenres` | array |  | ["all"] |  | Chart categories: One chart per category (and per chart and country). iPhone and iPad only; Mac charts are overall. |
| `developers` | array |  |  |  | Developers: Developer page URLs (https://apps.apple.com/us/developer/supercell/id488106216), numeric developer ids, or exact developer names as shown on the App Store. |
| `maxResults` | integer |  | 0 | 0– | Max apps per search / chart / developer / similar: 0 = everything the App Store lists (search up to 200, charts up to 100). |
| `includeFullDetails` | boolean |  | false |  | Full details for every listed app: Search, charts, developer and similar modes return an app card by default. Turn this on to get the full App details row (ratings histogram, version history, privacy labels, ...) for each app, charged as an app detail. |
| `includePrivacyLabels` | boolean |  | true |  | Include App Privacy labels: The app's privacy "nutrition label": data linked to you, data used to track you, and why. Free, it comes with the same request. |
| `includeVersionHistory` | boolean |  | true |  | Include version history: Recent versions with their dates and release notes. |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 6 | 1–20 | Parallel connections: How many IPs requests are spread over (the run's own IP plus proxy sessions). More is faster for very large review pulls. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)

```json
{
  "input": "top free iphone · all apps",
```

- all Apple App Store reviews of an app (more than 500, any country)

# Google Play Scraper: Reviews, App Details, Search & Charts

`wulfcare/google-play-scraper`: Scrape Google Play reviews (unlimited, any country and language, star and date filters), full app details with data safety and developer contacts, search results, top charts, developer apps and similar apps. Missing apps never crash a run.

**Use it for:**
- Google Play app details incl. data safety, installs, developer contacts
- Google Play search results, top charts, developer apps, similar apps
- Google Play reviews together with app data

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/google-play-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-play-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/google-play-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.0001 per review (review): One Google Play review with stars, text, date, helpful votes, app version and the developer reply. Not-found apps and failed requests are never charged.
- $0.0005 per app details (app-details): Full details of one app: ratings histogram, installs, price, developer contact, permissions, data safety, version and more.
- $0.0002 per app in a list (app-list-item): One app from a search, top chart, developer page or similar-apps list, with title, rating, installs, price and category.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-play-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"mode": "apps", "appIds": ["com.spotify.music"]}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/google-play-scraper").call(run_input={"mode": "apps", "appIds": ["com.spotify.music"]})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | yes | "reviews" | `reviews` (Reviews of apps), `apps` (App details (full)), `search` (Search results), `charts` (Top charts), `developer` (Apps by developer), `similar` (Similar apps) | What to scrape: Each run returns one kind of row, so your dataset always has the same columns. Reviews and App details use the app list below; the other modes use their own section. |
| `appIds` | array |  |  |  | Apps: Package names (com.spotify.music) or Google Play URLs (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.spotify.music). Used by Reviews, App details and Similar apps. |
| `country` | string |  | "us" |  | Country: Two-letter country code (us, gb, de, in, ng, br, ...). Prices, availability, charts and search results follow this country. |
| `language` | string |  | "en" |  | Language: Language code (en, de, es, pt-BR, ...). Google Play returns reviews written in this language, and app texts in it when the developer provides a translation. |
| `maxReviewsPerApp` | integer |  | 100 | 0– | Max reviews per app: 0 = every review Google Play has (it pages through them all). With a star filter the limit applies to each star rating separately. |
| `reviewsSort` | string |  | "newest" | `newest` (Newest first), `relevant` (Most relevant (Play default)) | Sort reviews by: Newest first is best for monitoring and date cutoffs. |
| `reviewStars` | array |  |  |  | Only these star ratings: Leave empty for all ratings. Filtering happens on Google Play's side, so asking for 1-star reviews doesn't cost you the others. |
| `reviewsSince` | string |  |  |  | Only reviews since: Stop at reviews older than this date, e.g. 2026-09-01 or "30 days". Fastest with "Newest first". |
| `includeReviewerNames` | boolean |  | false |  | Include reviewer display names: Off by default. Reviewer ids and profile pictures are never collected. |
| `searchQueries` | array |  |  |  | Search terms: One search per line, e.g. "budget tracker". Google Play's website shows up to about 30 apps per search. |
| `chartCollections` | array |  | ["topselling_free"] |  | Charts: Which top charts to fetch (up to 200 apps each). |
| `chartCategories` | array |  | ["APPLICATION"] |  | Chart categories: Every chart is fetched for every category picked here. |
| `developers` | array |  |  |  | Developers: Developer names exactly as on Google Play ("Spotify AB"), numeric developer ids, or developer page URLs. |
| `maxResults` | integer |  | 0 | 0– | Max apps per search / chart / developer: 0 = everything Google Play shows (search ~30, charts 200, similar ~50). |
| `includeFullDetails` | boolean |  | false |  | Full details for every listed app: Search, charts, developer and similar modes return a compact card by default. Turn this on to get the full App details row (ratings histogram, developer contact, data safety, ...) for each app, charged as an app detail. |
| `includeDataSafety` | boolean |  | true |  | Include data safety section: What data the app collects and shares, for what purpose, and its security practices. Free, it comes with the same request. |
| `includeDescriptionHtml` | boolean |  | false |  | Also include description HTML: The plain-text description is always included. Turn on to also get the original HTML. |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 5 | 1–20 | Parallel requests: How many apps or searches are fetched at the same time. |

# Google Play Reviews Scraper: All Reviews, No Cap

`wulfcare/google-play-reviews-scraper`: Scrape every Google Play review of any app, with no 150/1,000 cap: newest or most relevant, star and date filters, helpful votes, app versions and developer replies, any country and language. $0.10 per 1,000 reviews, no start fee, errors free.

**Use it for:**
- all Google Play reviews of an app, any country and language

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/google-play-reviews-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-play-reviews-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/google-play-reviews-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.0001 per review (review): One Google Play review with stars, text, date, helpful votes, the app version and the developer reply. Not-found apps and failed requests are never charged.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-play-reviews-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"appIds": ["com.spotify.music"], "country": "us", "maxReviewsPerApp": 1000}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/google-play-reviews-scraper").call(run_input={"appIds": ["com.spotify.music"], "country": "us", "maxReviewsPerApp": 1000})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `appIds` | array | yes |  |  | Apps: Package names (com.spotify.music) or Google Play URLs (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.spotify.music). Every review of each app is fetched, up to the limit below. |
| `country` | string |  | "us" |  | Country: Two-letter country code (us, gb, de, in, ng, br, ...). Prices, availability, charts and search results follow this country. |
| `language` | string |  | "en" |  | Language: Language code (en, de, es, pt-BR, ...). Google Play returns reviews written in this language, and app texts in it when the developer provides a translation. |
| `maxReviewsPerApp` | integer |  | 100 | 0– | Max reviews per app: 0 = every review Google Play has (it pages through them all). With a star filter the limit applies to each star rating separately. |
| `reviewsSort` | string |  | "newest" | `newest` (Newest first), `relevant` (Most relevant (Play default)) | Sort reviews by: Newest first is best for monitoring and date cutoffs. |
| `reviewStars` | array |  |  |  | Only these star ratings: Leave empty for all ratings. Filtering happens on Google Play's side, so asking for 1-star reviews doesn't cost you the others. |
| `reviewsSince` | string |  |  |  | Only reviews since: Stop at reviews older than this date, e.g. 2026-09-01 or "30 days". Fastest with "Newest first". |
| `includeReviewerNames` | boolean |  | false |  | Include reviewer display names: Off by default. Reviewer ids and profile pictures are never collected. |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 5 | 1–20 | Parallel requests: How many apps or searches are fetched at the same time. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)

```json
{
  "appId": "com.spotify.music",
  "appTitle": "Spotify: Music and Podcasts",
  "reviewId": "f35184e9-2cd7-4be2-aa3e-4aabd9f0df4f",
  "reviewUrl": "https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.spotify.music&reviewId=f35184e9-2cd7-4be2-aa3e-4aabd9f0df4f&hl=en&gl=us",
  "score": 5,
  "text": "i like it cuz it can make me relax",
  "date": "2026-11-08T23:33:31Z",
  "thumbsUp": 0,
  "appVersion": null,
  "replyText": null,
  "replyDate": null,
  "country": "US",
  "language": "en",
  "error": null
}
```

Results are what the source showed at run time and can contain errors; check anything important before relying on it.

# ChatGPT Search Scraper & AI Brand Visibility Tracker

`wulfcare/chatgpt-search-scraper`: Ask ChatGPT (with web search) your prompts for $0.05 per answer (Apify's own scraper: $0.20). Get the full answer, every cited source, every brand and product ChatGPT recommends (price, rating, reviews), its follow-up questions, and a free brand rank and citation report. No login.

**Use it for:**
- what ChatGPT (with web search) answers to a prompt, with cited sources and recommended products
- whether ChatGPT mentions / recommends / cites a brand vs competitors

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/chatgpt-search-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~chatgpt-search-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/chatgpt-search-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.05 per chatgpt answer (answer): One ChatGPT answer to one prompt, with every cited source and the brand report. Prompts ChatGPT didn't answer are never charged.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~chatgpt-search-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompts": ["What is the best CRM for a small business?"], "yourBrand": "HubSpot, hubspot.com", "competitors": ["Salesforce, salesforce.com", "Pipedrive, pipedrive.com"]}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/chatgpt-search-scraper").call(run_input={"prompts": ["What is the best CRM for a small business?"], "yourBrand": "HubSpot, hubspot.com", "competitors": ["Salesforce, salesforce.com", "Pipedrive, pipedrive.com"]})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prompts` | array | yes |  |  | Prompts: What to ask ChatGPT, one prompt per line. Write them the way your customers would ask, e.g. "best accounting software for a plumber". Each prompt is asked in a new, logged-out ChatGPT chat. |
| `yourBrand` | string |  |  |  | Your brand: Optional. Your brand name, then any other names and your website, separated by commas: "HubSpot, HubSpot CRM, hubspot.com". Every answer then says whether it mentions you, your rank against the competitors below, and whether it cites your site. |
| `competitors` | array |  |  |  | Competitors: Optional. Other brands to track, one per line, in the same format: name, other names, website. |
| `repeats` | integer |  | 1 | 1–10 | Ask each prompt this many times: ChatGPT words its answer differently each time, and the brands it names can change too. Ask the same prompt 3-5 times to get your share of mentions instead of a single snapshot. Every answer is its own row (and its own charge). |
| `webSearch` | boolean |  | true |  | Use web search: On (recommended): ChatGPT searches the web and cites sources, like it does for most product questions. Off: ChatGPT decides for itself whether to search. |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 2 | 1–4 | Prompts at a time: How many chats run in parallel. 2 is a safe default; 3-4 is faster but needs 4 GB of memory. |
| `language` | string |  |  |  | Browser language: Optional, e.g. en-GB, de-DE, fr-FR (default en-US). ChatGPT usually answers in the language of the prompt anyway. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)

# Gemini Search Scraper & AI Brand Visibility Tracker ($1/1k)

`wulfcare/gemini-search-scraper`: Ask Google Gemini your prompts: get the full answer (tables and steps included), every cited source, products with prices, and a brand report: mentioned or not, rank vs competitors, own site cited. No login, API key or browser. $1 per 1,000 answers, the lowest Gemini price on Apify.

**Use it for:**
- what Google Gemini answers to a prompt, with sources, and whether it mentions a brand

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/gemini-search-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~gemini-search-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/gemini-search-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.001 per gemini answer (gemini-answer): One Gemini answer to one prompt, with every source, products and the brand report. Prompts Gemini didn't answer are never charged.
- $0.002 per residential proxy (per answer) (residential-proxy-answer): Extra per answer only when you turn on Apify Proxy with the Residential group, to cover its bandwidth.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~gemini-search-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompts": ["What is the best CRM for a small business?"], "yourBrand": "HubSpot, hubspot.com", "competitors": ["Salesforce, salesforce.com", "Pipedrive, pipedrive.com"]}'
```


## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prompts` | array | yes |  |  | Prompts: What to ask Gemini, one prompt per line. Write them the way your customers would ask, e.g. "best accounting software for a plumber". Each prompt is asked in a new, logged-out Gemini chat. |

# Google AI Mode Scraper & AI Brand Visibility Tracker

`wulfcare/google-ai-mode-scraper`: Ask Google AI Mode your prompts: get the full answer (tables included), every cited source, and a brand report: mentioned or not, rank vs competitors, own site cited. Any country. No login, API key or proxy needed.

**Use it for:**
- what Google AI Mode answers to a prompt, with sources, and whether it mentions a brand

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/google-ai-mode-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-ai-mode-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/google-ai-mode-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.0045 per ai mode answer (ai-mode-answer): One Google AI Mode answer to one prompt, with every source and the brand report. Prompts AI Mode didn't answer are never charged.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-ai-mode-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompts": ["What is the best CRM for a small business?"], "yourBrand": "HubSpot, hubspot.com", "competitors": ["Salesforce, salesforce.com", "Pipedrive, pipedrive.com"]}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient

run = client.actor("wulfcare/google-ai-mode-scraper").call(run_input={"prompts": ["What is the best CRM for a small business?"], "yourBrand": "HubSpot, hubspot.com", "competitors": ["Salesforce, salesforce.com", "Pipedrive, pipedrive.com"]})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+

```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prompts` | array | yes |  |  | Prompts: What to ask Google AI Mode, one prompt per line. Write them the way your customers would search, e.g. "best accounting software for a plumber". Each prompt is asked in a new, logged-out AI Mode search. |
| `yourBrand` | string |  |  |  | Your brand: Optional. Your brand name, then any other names and your website, separated by commas: "HubSpot, HubSpot CRM, hubspot.com". Every answer then says whether it mentions you, your rank against the competitors below, and whether it cites your site. |
| `competitors` | array |  |  |  | Competitors: Optional. Other brands to track, one per line, in the same format: name, other names, website. |
| `repeats` | integer |  | 1 | 1–10 | Ask each prompt this many times: AI Mode words its answer differently each time, and the brands it names can change too. Ask the same prompt 3-5 times to get your share of mentions instead of a single snapshot. Every answer is its own row (and its own charge). |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 2 | 1–5 | Prompts at a time: How many questions run in parallel (each is a browser tab). 2 is the safe default: Google slows down busy IP addresses. |
| `language` | string |  | "en" |  | Language: Google interface language (hl), e.g. en, de, fr, es, ja. Default en. |
| `country` | string |  | "US" | `US` (United States), `GB` (United Kingdom), `CA` (Canada), `AU` (Australia), `NZ` (New Zealand), `IE` (Ireland), `IN` (India), `DE` (Germany), `FR` (France), `ES` (Spain), `IT` (Italy), `NL` (Netherlands), `JP` (Japan), `BR` (Brazil), `MX` (Mexico), `SG` (Singapore), `ZA` (South Africa) | Country: Google country (gl) for the search. AI Mode leans on that country's sites and shops for local questions. |

# Microsoft Copilot Search Scraper & AI Brand Visibility Tracker

`wulfcare/copilot-search-scraper`: Ask Microsoft Copilot Search (Bing) your prompts: get the full answer as markdown, every cited source with title and snippet, and a brand report: mentioned or not, rank vs competitors, own site cited. No login or API key.

**Use it for:**
- what Microsoft Copilot Search (Bing) answers to a prompt, with sources, and whether it mentions a brand

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/copilot-search-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~copilot-search-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/copilot-search-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.008 per copilot answer (copilot-answer): One Microsoft Copilot answer to one prompt, with every source and the brand report. Prompts Copilot didn't answer are never charged.
- $0.008 per residential proxy (per answer) (residential-proxy-answer): Extra per answer only when it went through Apify's residential proxy (Bing refused the server's IP address, or you chose a country), to cover its bandwidth.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~copilot-search-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompts": ["What is the best CRM for a small business?"], "yourBrand": "HubSpot, hubspot.com", "competitors": ["Salesforce, salesforce.com", "Pipedrive, pipedrive.com"]}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/copilot-search-scraper").call(run_input={"prompts": ["What is the best CRM for a small business?"], "yourBrand": "HubSpot, hubspot.com", "competitors": ["Salesforce, salesforce.com", "Pipedrive, pipedrive.com"]})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prompts` | array | yes |  |  | Prompts: What to ask Copilot, one prompt per line. Write them the way your customers would ask, e.g. "best accounting software for a plumber". Each prompt is asked in a new, logged-out Copilot Search. |
| `yourBrand` | string |  |  |  | Your brand: Optional. Your brand name, then any other names and your website, separated by commas: "HubSpot, HubSpot CRM, hubspot.com". Every answer then says whether it mentions you, your rank against the competitors below, and whether it cites your site. |
| `competitors` | array |  |  |  | Competitors: Optional. Other brands to track, one per line, in the same format: name, other names, website. |
| `repeats` | integer |  | 1 | 1–10 | Ask each prompt this many times: Copilot words its answer differently each time, and the brands it names can change too. Ask the same prompt 3-5 times to get your share of mentions instead of a single snapshot. Every answer is its own row (and its own charge). |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 3 | 1–8 | Prompts at a time: How many questions run in parallel (each is a browser tab). 3 is a safe default. |
| `language` | string |  | "en" |  | Language: Interface language code, e.g. en, de, fr, es, ja (default en). Copilot usually answers in the language of the prompt anyway. |
| `useResidentialProxy` | boolean |  | false |  | Always use residential proxy: Off (recommended): questions go out from the Apify server's own IP address (in the US), and the run switches to Apify residential proxy by itself only if Bing starts asking for captchas. Turn on to ask from a home IP in the country below, e.g. to see what Copilot tells people in that country. Answers through residential proxy cost an extra residential-proxy-answer event (it covers the bandwidth). |
| `proxyCountry` | string |  | "US" | `US` (United States), `GB` (United Kingdom), `CA` (Canada), `AU` (Australia), `DE` (Germany), `FR` (France), `ES` (Spain), `IT` (Italy), `NL` (Netherlands), `IN` (India), `JP` (Japan), `BR` (Brazil), `MX` (Mexico) | Residential proxy country: Where residential-proxy questions come from. Copilot tailors local answers (shops, prices, places) to it. |

# AI Visibility Tracker: ChatGPT, Gemini & Google AI Overviews

`wulfcare/ai-visibility-tracker`: See whether ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews recommend your brand or your competitors. Get a visibility score, share of voice, the prompts you're missing from, the sites AI cites, and a white-label HTML report. $0.04 per answer, report free. No API keys.

**Use it for:**
- AI visibility / share of voice of a brand across ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews in one run, with HTML report

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/ai-visibility-tracker
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~ai-visibility-tracker/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/ai-visibility-tracker`

**Price:**
- $0.04 per ai answer (ai-answer): One answer from one AI engine (ChatGPT, Gemini or Google AI Overview) to one prompt, with its brand analysis. Searches with no AI Overview, failed prompts and the report are never charged.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~ai-visibility-tracker/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"yourBrand": "Pipedrive, pipedrive.com", "competitors": ["HubSpot, hubspot.com", "Salesforce, salesforce.com"], "category": "CRM for small business", "promptCount": 5}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/ai-visibility-tracker").call(run_input={"yourBrand": "Pipedrive, pipedrive.com", "competitors": ["HubSpot, hubspot.com", "Salesforce, salesforce.com"], "category": "CRM for small business", "promptCount": 5})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `yourBrand` | string |  |  |  | Your brand: Your brand name, then any other names and your website, separated by commas: "Pipedrive, Pipedrive CRM, pipedrive.com". The report scores how often and how high AI recommends you, and whether it cites your site. Leave empty to just see who AI recommends. |
| `competitors` | array |  |  |  | Competitors: The brands you compete with, one per line, in the same format: name, other names, website. Their scores and share of voice sit next to yours in the report. |
| `category` | string |  |  |  | Category (writes the prompts for you): What you sell, the way a customer would put it: "CRM for small business", "dentist in Brisbane", "running shoes for flat feet". The Actor writes the buyer questions people ask AI ("What is the best ...?", "Which ... would you recommend?", "alternatives to "). Use it, your own prompts below, or both. |
| `promptCount` | integer |  | 10 | 1–50 | Number of prompts to write: How many questions to write from the category (1-50). Each is asked once on every engine you pick. |
| `prompts` | array |  |  |  | Your own prompts: Optional. Exact questions to ask, one per line, e.g. "best CRM for a real estate agency". Prompts that name a tracked brand ("Is HubSpot good?") are answered and shown, but left out of the scores, since they name the brand whatever its visibility. |
| `engines` | array |  | ["chatgpt", "gemini", "google_ai_overview"] |  | AI engines: Where to ask. Every engine is asked as a new, logged-out visitor, so you see what your customers see, not an API answer. |
| `country` | string |  | "US" | `US` (United States), `GB` (United Kingdom), `AU` (Australia), `CA` (Canada), `NZ` (New Zealand), `IE` (Ireland), `IN` (India), `SG` (Singapore), `ZA` (South Africa), `DE` (Germany), `FR` (France), `ES` (Spain), `IT` (Italy), `NL` (Netherlands), `SE` (Sweden), `PL` (Poland), `BR` (Brazil), `MX` (Mexico), `JP` (Japan), `AE` (United Arab Emirates) | Country: Where your customers are. Google AI Overviews are searched for this country. ChatGPT is asked through a residential IP address in this country when it isn't the US (this uses your Apify residential proxy). Gemini doesn't localise logged-out answers by country. |
| `language` | string |  | "en" |  | Language: Two-letter language code for Google and the browser (en, de, fr, es, ...). Write your prompts in the same language. |
| `repeats` | integer |  | 1 | 1–5 | Ask each prompt this many times: AI answers change between askings. Asking each prompt 2-3 times gives steadier scores. Every answer is its own row and its own charge. |
| `maxRunMinutes` | integer |  |  | 1–600 | Stop asking after (minutes): When time is up, no more prompts are asked and the report is written from the answers so far. Leave empty to ask everything. The run also stops in time before its own timeout. |
| `projectName` | string |  |  |  | Project name (tracks changes over time): Optional. Give the brand or client a name, e.g. "acme-weekly", and schedule this Actor (weekly is typical). Each run is saved under the name in your account, and the report shows the score trend and the prompts you gained or lost since the last run. |
| `reportTitle` | string |  |  |  | Report title: Optional. Heading of the HTML report (default: "AI Visibility Report: "). |
| `agencyName` | string |  |  |  | Prepared by (agency name): Optional. Shown on the HTML report as "Prepared by ...", for agencies sending it to clients. The report carries no Apify branding. |

# Google Trends Trending Now Scraper: Every Trending Search

`wulfcare/google-trends-trending-now`: Every search trending on Google right now, for any country: search volume, % increase, start time, related searches and news articles. 4/24/48/168-hour windows, categories, many countries per run. $0.30 per 1,000 trends, no start fee.

**Use it for:**
- every search trending on Google right now in one or many countries, with search volume, % increase, related searches and news
- cheapest way to get Trending Now only (no keyword reports)

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/google-trends-trending-now
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-trends-trending-now/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/google-trends-trending-now`

**Price:**
- $0.0003 per trending search (trending-item): One trending search from Trending Now, with volume, growth, related searches and category. Failed countries are never charged.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~google-trends-trending-now/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"trendingGeos": ["US"]}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/google-trends-trending-now").call(run_input={"trendingGeos": ["US"]})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `trendingGeos` | array |  |  |  | Countries or regions: ISO codes like US, GB, AU, or regions like US-CA. One set of trends per entry. |
| `trendingHours` | string |  | "24" | `4` (Past 4 hours), `24` (Past 24 hours), `48` (Past 48 hours), `168` (Past 7 days) | Time window: How far back to look for trending searches. |
| `trendingCategories` | array |  |  |  | Only these categories (optional): Leave empty for all categories. |
| `trendingActiveOnly` | boolean |  | false |  | Only trends that are still active: Skip trends that have already ended. |
| `maxTrendsPerGeo` | integer |  | 0 | 0– | Max trends per country (0 = all): Trends are sorted by search volume, highest first. |
| `language` | string |  | "en-US" |  | Interface language: Language of Google's labels and related queries, e.g. en-US, en-GB, de, ja. |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 3 | 1–10 | Parallel reports: How many reports run at once, each on its own IP. Only applies when using a proxy. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)


`wulfcare/youtube-shorts-scraper`: Scrape YouTube Shorts from search terms and channels: views, likes, comment count, publish date, description, hashtags, plus channel subscribers. No login, no API key. $0.50 per 1,000 Shorts, no start fee.

**Use it for:**
- YouTube Shorts from search terms or channels with views, likes, comment count, publish date and hashtags

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/youtube-shorts-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~youtube-shorts-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/youtube-shorts-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.0005 per short (video): One YouTube Short with all its details. Errors and not-found inputs are never charged. No start fee.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~youtube-shorts-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"searchQueries": ["cooking hacks"], "maxResultsShorts": 20}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/youtube-shorts-scraper").call(run_input={"searchQueries": ["cooking hacks"], "maxResultsShorts": 20})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `searchQueries` | array |  |  |  | Search terms: What you would type in YouTube's search box. Each term is searched with YouTube's Shorts filter and gets up to "Maximum Shorts" results. |
| `maxResultsShorts` | integer |  | 50 | 1–999999 | Maximum Shorts per search term or channel: Shorts to get from each search term and each channel (its Shorts tab). |
| `startUrls` | array |  | [] |  | Direct URLs: Channels (@handle, /channel/UC..., /@name/shorts) to get their Shorts tab, or Shorts URLs (youtube.com/shorts/ID) to get those Shorts. |
| `sortingOrder` | string |  |  | `relevance` (Relevance), `rating` (Rating), `date` (Upload date), `views` (View count) | Sorting order: How YouTube orders the search results. YouTube doesn't follow "Upload date" strictly. |
| `dateFilter` | string |  |  | `hour` (Last hour), `today` (Today), `week` (This week), `month` (This month), `year` (This year) | Upload date: Only videos uploaded within this time. |
| `oldestPostDate` | string |  |  |  | Only videos published on or after: A date (2026-01-31) or an age ("7 days", "2 weeks", "3 months", "1 year"). Works for every source. On a channel listed newest first the run stops at the first older video; elsewhere older videos are skipped. |
| `sortVideosBy` | string |  | "NEWEST" | `NEWEST` (Newest), `POPULAR` (Popular), `OLDEST` (Oldest) | Channel order: The order of a channel's videos, Shorts and streams (the channel page's Latest / Popular / Oldest buttons). |
| `includeVideoDetails` | boolean |  | true |  | Open every video (likes, comments, exact date, description, tags...): On: each video's likes, comment count, exact publish time, full description with its links, hashtags, category, tags and more. Off: only what the list shows (title, views, duration, "3 days ago"), several times faster. Video URLs are always opened. |
| `includeChannelInfo` | boolean |  | true |  | Add channel info to each video: The channel's subscribers, total views, video count, country, joined date, description, links, avatar and banner, on every row (one small request per channel). |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 10 | 1–30 | Videos at a time: How many videos are fetched in parallel. |
