# Flight Price Tracker: Price Drop Alerts from Google Flights

`wulfcare/flight-price-tracker`: Track flight prices on any route: schedule it and every run says which fares dropped or rose, which flights are new or gone, the all-time low and if a fare is under your target. Google Flights data. $0.15 per 1,000 flights, no start fee.

**Use it for:**
- scheduled flight price checks that say which fares dropped or rose, new or gone flights, the all-time low and whether a fare is under a target

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/flight-price-tracker
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~flight-price-tracker/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/flight-price-tracker`

**Price:**
- $0.00015 per result (result): One row: a route-and-date summary (lowest price, Google's verdict, changes since the last run), one flight, or one date's cheapest price. Errors and 'gone' rows are free.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~flight-price-tracker/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"origin": "JFK", "destination": "LAX", "departureDate": "+30 days"}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/flight-price-tracker").call(run_input={"origin": "JFK", "destination": "LAX", "departureDate": "+30 days"})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `origin` | string |  |  |  | From (airport code): IATA code of the departure airport, e.g. JFK. Several, comma-separated, to search them together: JFK,LGA,EWR. |
| `destination` | string |  |  |  | To (airport code): IATA code of the arrival airport, e.g. LAX (or several: LAX,BUR,LGB). |
| `departureDate` | string |  |  |  | Departure date: YYYY-MM-DD, or relative: "+30 days", "in 2 weeks", "tomorrow". Empty = in 30 days. |
| `returnDate` | string |  |  |  | Return date (round trip): Empty = one way. YYYY-MM-DD, or "+7 days" counted from the departure date. Round-trip prices are for the whole trip, as on Google Flights. |
| `tripDays` | integer |  |  | 0–330 | Trip length in days (round trip): Instead of a return date: return this many days after departure. 0 = one way. |
| `routes` | array |  |  |  | More routes: Extra routes, one per line: "SYD-LAX", "JFK,EWR-LHR", "MEL to AKL". Each is searched for the same dates and options. |
| `departureDays` | integer |  | 1 | 1–60 | Departure dates in a row: Search this many consecutive departure dates from the first (full flight lists for each). For just the cheapest price per date over a long range, use "Cheapest dates" instead. |
| `maxFlights` | integer |  | 20 | 0–500 | Flights per search: Flight rows per route and date: Google's "best" flights first, then the rest by price. Google lists 50-300. 0 = just the summary row (lowest price, verdict, trip cost). |
| `cabinClass` | string |  | "economy" | `economy` (Economy), `premium-economy` (Premium economy), `business` (Business), `first` (First) | Cabin: Seat class. |
| `adults` | integer |  | 1 | 1–9 | Adults: Prices are the total for all passengers. |
| `children` | integer |  | 0 | 0–8 | Children (2-11): Children aged 2-11 (count toward the total price). |
| `maxStops` | string |  | "any" | `any` (Any), `nonstop` (Nonstop only), `1` (1 stop or fewer), `2` (2 stops or fewer) | Stops: Most stops a flight may have. |
| `currency` | string |  | "USD" |  | Currency: Three-letter code: USD, EUR, GBP, AUD, INR... Google prices directly in it. |
| `trackerName` | string |  | "default" |  | Tracker name: Keep separate trackers apart (e.g. "client-a", "summer-trip"). Letters, digits, dashes. |
| `onlyChanges` | boolean |  | false |  | Only output changes: With tracking: output only flights that are new or changed price (plus one summary row per search). You pay only for those rows, so daily monitoring costs almost nothing. |
| `targetPrice` | integer |  |  | 0– | Target price: Optional: the summary's belowTargetPrice is true when the lowest price is at or under this (in the chosen currency). Handy for alerts and webhooks. |
| `cheapestDates` | boolean |  | false |  | Cheapest dates: Also output the cheapest price for every departure date in a range (Google's date grid), one row per date, the cheapest flagged. Round trips keep the same trip length. |
| `cheapestDatesRange` | integer |  | 60 | 7–330 | Days to scan: Departure dates from the departure date on. |
| `language` | string |  | "en" |  | Language: Language of airport and airline names (hl=). |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 6 | 1–20 | Requests at once: Searches sent to Google at the same time. |
| `residentialFallback` | boolean |  | true |  | Fall back to residential proxy: With the default Apify Proxy: when Google keeps refusing datacenter IPs, finish the run on US residential IPs (no extra charge to you). |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)


# Steam Reviews Scraper: All Reviews, Any Game, No Key

`wulfcare/steam-reviews-scraper`: Scrape every Steam review of any game, with no cap and no API key: newest/helpful sort, positive/negative, any language, playtime, votes, Steam Deck and developer replies. $0.10 per 1,000 reviews, no start fee, errors free.

**Use it for:**
- every Steam review of a game (any language, no API key) with votes, playtime, Steam Deck flag and developer replies

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/steam-reviews-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~steam-reviews-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/steam-reviews-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.0001 per review (review): One Steam review with the recommendation, text, date, playtime, votes and the developer reply. Games not found and failed requests are never charged.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~steam-reviews-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"appIds": ["1145360"], "maxReviewsPerApp": 200}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/steam-reviews-scraper").call(run_input={"appIds": ["1145360"], "maxReviewsPerApp": 200})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `appIds` | array | yes |  |  | Games: Steam app ids (1145360), store URLs (https://store.steampowered.com/app/1145360/) or game names (the best match on Steam is used). Every review of each game is fetched, up to the limit below. |
| `maxReviewsPerApp` | integer |  | 1000 | 0– | Maximum reviews per game: 0 = every review the game has (big games have hundreds of thousands). |
| `reviewsSort` | string |  | "newest" | `newest` (Newest first), `helpful` (Most helpful first), `updated` (Recently updated first) | Order: Newest first can also stop at a date (below). |
| `reviewType` | string |  | "all" | `all` (All), `positive` (Positive (recommended) only), `negative` (Negative (not recommended) only) | Reviews: Positive = the reviewer recommends the game (thumbs up). Filtered on Steam's side, so you only pay for the reviews you want. |
| `languages` | array |  | ["all"] |  | Languages: "all", or Steam language names like english, schinese, russian, spanish, brazilian, german, french, japanese, koreana. |
| `purchaseType` | string |  | "all" | `all` (Everyone (incl. free-to-play and gifted)), `steam` (Bought on Steam only), `key` (Activated with a key only) | Who wrote them: Everyone matches the review counts on free-to-play games. "Bought on Steam only" matches the default count on a paid game's store page. |
| `reviewsSince` | string |  |  |  | Only reviews since: Skip reviews older than this, e.g. 2026-09-01 or "30 days". The run stops as soon as it reaches older reviews (uses Newest first). |
| `includeReviewerIds` | boolean |  | false |  | Include reviewer Steam IDs: Off by default. On: each row gets the reviewer's public Steam ID and a link to the review. |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 5 | 1–20 | Games at a time: Each game's reviews are read page by page; this many games run in parallel. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)


# Shopify App Store Reviews Scraper: Every Review, No Cap

`wulfcare/shopify-app-store-reviews-scraper`: Scrape every review of any Shopify App Store app: stars, text, date, the merchant's store name and country, time using the app and the developer's reply. Star and date filters. $0.03 per 1,000 reviews, no start fee, errors free.

**Use it for:**
- every review of a Shopify App Store app with stars, date, merchant store and country, time using the app and developer reply

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/shopify-app-store-reviews-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~shopify-app-store-reviews-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/shopify-app-store-reviews-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.000025 per review (review): One Shopify App Store review with stars, text, date, the store name and country, and the developer reply. Apps not found and failed requests are never charged.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~shopify-app-store-reviews-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"apps": ["judgeme"], "maxReviewsPerApp": 200}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/shopify-app-store-reviews-scraper").call(run_input={"apps": ["judgeme"], "maxReviewsPerApp": 200})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `apps` | array | yes |  |  | Apps: Shopify App Store apps: the handle from the app's URL (judgeme for apps.shopify.com/judgeme) or the full URL. Every review of each app is fetched, up to the limit below. |
| `maxReviewsPerApp` | integer |  | 1000 | 0– | Maximum reviews per app: 0 = every review the app has (the biggest apps have 50,000+). |
| `reviewsSort` | string |  | "newest" | `newest` (Newest first), `relevant` (Most relevant (Shopify's default)) | Order: Newest first can also stop at a date (below). |
| `reviewStars` | array |  |  |  | Star ratings: Only reviews with these ratings, e.g. 1 and 2 for complaints. Filtered on Shopify's side, so you only pay for the reviews you want. Empty = all. |
| `reviewsSince` | string |  |  |  | Only reviews since: Skip reviews older than this, e.g. 2026-09-01 or "30 days". The run stops as soon as it reaches older reviews (uses Newest first). |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 8 | 1–20 | Proxy IPs at a time: Review pages are spread over this many Apify Proxy IPs, each read at Shopify's polite rate. Ignored with the proxy off. |

## Output: one dataset item (real run, long values trimmed)


# Bing Copilot Scraper: Answers, Citations & Brand Mentions

`wulfcare/bing-copilot-scraper`: Ask Bing Copilot (Microsoft Copilot Search) any prompts: the full answer as markdown, every cited source with title and snippet, and whether your brand is mentioned or cited. $3 per 1,000 answers ($10 when a residential proxy is needed), no start fee.

**Use it for:**
- what Bing Copilot answers to a prompt as markdown, with cited sources, and whether a brand is mentioned or cited

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/bing-copilot-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~bing-copilot-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/bing-copilot-scraper`

**Price:**
- $0.003 per copilot answer (copilot-answer): One Bing Copilot answer to one prompt, with every source and the brand report. Prompts Copilot didn't answer are never charged.
- $0.008 per residential proxy (per answer) (residential-proxy-answer): Extra per answer only when it went through Apify's residential proxy (Bing refused the server's IP address, or you chose a country), to cover its bandwidth.

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~bing-copilot-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"prompts": ["What is the best CRM for a small business?"], "yourBrand": "HubSpot, hubspot.com", "competitors": ["Salesforce, salesforce.com", "Pipedrive, pipedrive.com"]}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/bing-copilot-scraper").call(run_input={"prompts": ["What is the best CRM for a small business?"], "yourBrand": "HubSpot, hubspot.com", "competitors": ["Salesforce, salesforce.com", "Pipedrive, pipedrive.com"]})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prompts` | array | yes |  |  | Prompts: What to ask Copilot, one prompt per line. Write them the way your customers would ask, e.g. "best accounting software for a plumber". Each prompt is asked in a new, logged-out Copilot Search. |
| `yourBrand` | string |  |  |  | Your brand: Optional. Your brand name, then any other names and your website, separated by commas: "HubSpot, HubSpot CRM, hubspot.com". Every answer then says whether it mentions you, your rank against the competitors below, and whether it cites your site. |
| `competitors` | array |  |  |  | Competitors: Optional. Other brands to track, one per line, in the same format: name, other names, website. |
| `repeats` | integer |  | 1 | 1–10 | Ask each prompt this many times: Copilot words its answer differently each time, and the brands it names can change too. Ask the same prompt 3-5 times to get your share of mentions instead of a single snapshot. Every answer is its own row (and its own charge). |
| `maxConcurrency` | integer |  | 3 | 1–8 | Prompts at a time: How many questions run in parallel (each is a browser tab). 3 is a safe default. |
| `language` | string |  | "en" |  | Language: Interface language code, e.g. en, de, fr, es, ja (default en). Copilot usually answers in the language of the prompt anyway. |
| `useResidentialProxy` | boolean |  | false |  | Always use residential proxy: Off (recommended): questions go out from the Apify server's own IP address (in the US), and the run switches to Apify residential proxy by itself only if Bing starts asking for captchas. Turn on to ask from a home IP in the country below, e.g. to see what Copilot tells people in that country. Answers through residential proxy cost an extra residential-proxy-answer event (it covers the bandwidth). |
| `proxyCountry` | string |  | "US" | `US` (United States), `GB` (United Kingdom), `CA` (Canada), `AU` (Australia), `DE` (Germany), `FR` (France), `ES` (Spain), `IT` (Italy), `NL` (Netherlands), `IN` (India), `JP` (Japan), `BR` (Brazil), `MX` (Mexico) | Residential proxy country: Where residential-proxy questions come from. Copilot tailors local answers (shops, prices, places) to it. |

# AI Training Jobs: Mercor, Outlier, DataAnnotation, Alignerr +11

`wulfcare/ai-training-jobs-scraper`: AI trainer, AI tutor and data-annotation jobs from 15 platforms: Mercor, Alignerr, Outlier, DataAnnotation, Mindrift, Meridial (Invisible), Turing, micro1, Welo Data, OneForma, xAI, Handshake AI, Appen and more. Pay as numbers, location, date, apply link. Only-new-jobs mode.

**Use it for:**
- AI training, AI tutor and data annotation job listings (Mercor, Outlier, DataAnnotation, Alignerr, Turing and more)

- Store page: https://apify.com/wulfcare/ai-training-jobs-scraper
- OpenAPI spec: https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~ai-training-jobs-scraper/builds/default/openapi.json
- MCP: `https://mcp.apify.com?tools=wulfcare/ai-training-jobs-scraper`

**Price:**
- Free (only Apify platform usage, usually fractions of a cent)

## Call it

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.apify.com/v2/acts/wulfcare~ai-training-jobs-scraper/run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=$APIFY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"keywords": ["python"], "minHourlyRate": 30}'
```

```python
from apify_client import ApifyClient
client = ApifyClient(APIFY_TOKEN)
run = client.actor("wulfcare/ai-training-jobs-scraper").call(run_input={"keywords": ["python"], "minHourlyRate": 30})
dataset_id = run["defaultDatasetId"] if isinstance(run, dict) else run.default_dataset_id  # apify-client 1-2 vs 3+
items = list(client.dataset(dataset_id).iterate_items())
```

## Input

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Allowed values | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `platforms` | array |  | ["mercor", "alignerr", "micro1", "xai", "handshake", "appen", "remotasks", "humansignal", "outlier", "dataannotation", "mindrift", "meridial", "welo", "turing", "oneforma"] |  | Platforms: Which AI-training platforms to read. Leave empty for all of them. |
| `keywords` | array |  |  |  | Keywords: Return only jobs that mention at least one of these in the title, category, skills or client name (e.g. 'law', 'medicine', 'python', 'spanish'). Whole words: 'law' does not match 'lawn'. End a word with * to allow endings ('math*' matches math and mathematics). Leave empty for every job. |
| `excludeKeywords` | array |  |  |  | Exclude keywords: Drop jobs whose title, category or skills mention any of these (e.g. 'audio', 'transcription'). |
| `searchDescriptions` | boolean |  | false |  | Also search job descriptions: Match keywords inside the full job description too. Finds more jobs but also loose matches (a physics job that mentions 'laws of motion' would match 'law'). |
| `minHourlyRate` | integer |  |  | 0– | Minimum hourly pay (USD): Keep only hourly jobs whose top rate is at least this much. Jobs paid per task, one-off or without a stated rate are dropped when this is set. |
| `remoteOnly` | boolean |  | false |  | Remote only: Keep only jobs listed as remote. |
| `postedWithin` | string |  |  |  | Posted within: Only jobs first posted in this period, e.g. '24 hours', '7 days', '2 weeks', or since a date like 2026-09-01. Alignerr dates come from each job page (needs 'Full job details'). |
| `onlyNewJobs` | boolean |  | false |  | Only new jobs (for schedules): Return, and charge for, only jobs that earlier runs with the same filters have not returned yet. Perfect for a daily schedule that feeds Slack, email or a sheet. The list of seen jobs is kept in a key-value store named 'ai-training-jobs-monitor' in your own account. |
| `monitorName` | string |  |  |  | Monitor name: Optional. Runs with the same monitor name share one 'already seen' list. By default the list is tied to your platform and filter choices. |
| `maxJobs` | integer |  | 1000 | 0– | Maximum jobs: Stop after this many jobs (newest first). 0 = no limit. All platforms together have about 1,350 distinct jobs (about 6,400 with every Alignerr city listing). |
| `includeDescriptions` | boolean |  | true |  | Include job descriptions: Full job description text in each row. Turn off for smaller rows. |
| `fullDetails` | boolean |  | true |  | Full job details (Alignerr, micro1): Open the page of each returned Alignerr and micro1 job. Alignerr's list has only a short summary and no date; micro1's list has no description or number of openings. Turn off for a faster run with less detail. |
| `alignerrAllLocations` | boolean |  | false |  | Every Alignerr city listing: Alignerr lists most remote roles once per city (one role can have 300+ identical copies). By default you get one row per role, with the number of copies in 'openings'. Turn on to get every copy as its own row (about 5,600). |
